You are a programming expert. 
        You will be provided with a patch used to fix a bug. 
        Based on the commit message and modifications in the patch, you need to analyze the root cause of the bug in detail. 

        Here is the patch content:
        From 193e87143c290ec16838f5368adc0e0bc94eb931 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Dan Carpenter <dan.carpenter@oracle.com>
Date: Thu, 13 Oct 2016 11:06:47 +0300
Subject: [PATCH] mtd: spi-nor: Off by one in cqspi_setup_flash()

There are CQSPI_MAX_CHIPSELECT elements in the ->f_pdata array so the >
should be >=.

Fixes: 140623410536 ('mtd: spi-nor: Add driver for Cadence Quad SPI Flash Controller')
Signed-off-by: Dan Carpenter <dan.carpenter@oracle.com>
Reviewed-by: Marek Vasut <marex@denx.de>
Signed-off-by: Cyrille Pitchen <cyrille.pitchen@atmel.com>
---
 drivers/mtd/spi-nor/cadence-quadspi.c | 2 +-
 1 file changed, 1 insertion(+), 1 deletion(-)

diff --git a/drivers/mtd/spi-nor/cadence-quadspi.c b/drivers/mtd/spi-nor/cadence-quadspi.c
index d403ba7b8f43..944863be0320 100644
--- a/drivers/mtd/spi-nor/cadence-quadspi.c
+++ b/drivers/mtd/spi-nor/cadence-quadspi.c
@@ -1082,7 +1082,7 @@ static int cqspi_setup_flash(struct cqspi_st *cqspi, struct device_node *np)
 			goto err;
 		}
 
-		if (cs > CQSPI_MAX_CHIPSELECT) {
+		if (cs >= CQSPI_MAX_CHIPSELECT) {
 			dev_err(dev, "Chip select %d out of range.\n", cs);
 			goto err;
 		}
-- 
2.25.1


        
        Provide a response strictly in the following format:
        Root cause:<Root cause>

Root cause: The bug was caused by an off-by-one error in the condition that checks if the chip select index (`cs`) is within the valid range. The original condition used `>` instead of `>=`, which allowed an invalid chip select index equal to `CQSPI_MAX_CHIPSELECT` to pass through, leading to potential out-of-bounds access in the `->f_pdata` array. The fix corrects this by changing the condition to `>=`, ensuring that the index is strictly less than `CQSPI_MAX_CHIPSELECT`.

The original condition used `>` instead of `>=`, which allowed an invalid chip select index equal to `CQSPI_MAX_CHIPSELECT` to pass through, leading to potential out-of-bounds access in the `->f_pdata` array. The fix corrects this by changing the condition to `>=`, ensuring that the index is strictly less than `CQSPI_MAX_CHIPSELECT`.
